html:
The Parkatêjê are a Timbira people of southeastern Pará in Brazil, speakers of a Gê language and close kin of the Canela and Krenyê. They are also called the Gavião of Pará.

They live in the Mãe Maria reserve near Marabá. In the 1900s their land was cut by roads, the Carajás railway, power lines and the Tucuruí dam, and contact brought epidemics. Like other Timbira, they hold log races, in which teams run carrying heavy sections of tree trunk.
